principle: Soldiers in your home: a 1776 grievance that became a 1791 right

thread.note: The Declaration lists quartering large bodies of armed troops among the king's abuses.
The Bill of Rights answers it directly: no soldier quartered in any house in peacetime without the owner's consent.

principle: Trial by jury: the complaint the Sixth and Seventh Amendments resolved

thread.note: The Declaration protests being deprived, in many cases, of the benefits of trial by jury.
A speedy public trial by an impartial jury in criminal cases.
The right to a jury extended to civil suits at common law.

principle: No taxation without consent: from grievance, to the taxing power, to the income tax

thread.note: Imposing taxes on the colonists without their consent.
The Constitution vests the taxing power in Congress, the people's elected representatives.
Later authorizes a federal income tax laid directly on incomes.

principle: Tried far from home: the grievance behind the right to a local jury

thread.note: Transporting the colonists beyond the seas to be tried for pretended offences.
Guarantees trial by a jury of the state and district where the crime was committed.

principle: Standing armies without consent: the fear that shaped Congress's war power and the Third Amendment

thread.note: The king kept standing armies among the colonists in peacetime without the consent of their legislatures.
The Constitution answers by placing the power to raise and fund armies with Congress, the elected legislature.
And forbids quartering those soldiers in private homes in peacetime without consent.

principle: Government by consent: from a self-evident truth to 'We the People'

thread.note: Governments derive their just powers from the consent of the governed.
The Constitution enacts that consent in its first three words: We the People.
Powers not delegated are reserved to the states, or to the people themselves.

principle: Self-rule: the grievance of suspended legislatures and the vesting of legislative power

thread.note: The king suspended the colonists' own legislatures and claimed the power to legislate for them.
The Constitution vests all legislative powers in a Congress elected by the people.

principle: All are created equal: a 1776 ideal, made enforceable law over the next 144 years

thread.note: We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal.
Turns the ideal into law: equal protection of the laws for every person.
The vote may not be denied on account of race, color, or previous servitude.
The vote may not be denied on account of sex.
